question: What was the performance of multilingual BERT?

answer.free_form_answer: BERT had 76.6 F1 macro score on x-stance dataset.
evidence: To put the supervised score into context we list scores that variants of Bert have achieved on other stance detection datasets in Table TABREF46. It seems that the supervised part of x-stance has a similar difficulty as the SemEval-2016 BIBREF0 or MPCHI BIBREF22 datasets on which Bert has previously been evaluated.

title: X-Stance: A Multilingual Multi-Target Dataset for Stance Detection
answer_short: Baseline results show that multilingual BERT performs moderately successfully in zero-shot cross-lingual and cross-target transfer.
answer_rationale: The performance of multilingual BERT is described in multiple documents. Text 2 states that the baseline accuracy is comparable to previous benchmarks with room for improvement. Text 10 explicitly states that baseline results show zero-shot cross-lingual and cross-target transfer is 'moderately successful'. Text 4 adds that M-Bert performs better than majority class baselines, even in zero-shot settings. Text 3 notes that while there is some capability for zero-shot transfer, there is a performance gap that future work could address. Collectively, these documents support the conclusion that multilingual BERT performs moderately successfully in cross-lingual and cross-target settings.
